samples.summary: `copyTitle` test 'only considers the titles it is given' is a restatement of the base case and asserts nothing about scoping
samples.evidence: `expect(copyTitle('Report', [])).toBe('Report (copy)')` is semantically identical to the first test (`['Report']` also contains no `Report (copy)`). `copyTitle` has no scoping logic at all — the scoping claim in the comment ("Titles from another folder / workspace are not passed in") is a property of the *caller* (DocumentCopyService's `documents({where:{workspaceId, folderId}})`), which this test never touches. The test passes regardless of whether folder scoping works.

samples.summary: No test asserts the Yorkie doc key prefix used by the JSON-root arm (sheet/slides/board)
samples.evidence: The `doc` arm test asserts `docKeyPrefix: 'doc-'` on every `withDocument` call, but every sheet test uses `makeYorkie`, whose mock branches only on `opts.syncMode` and ignores `docKeyPrefix` entirely (document-copy.service.spec.ts:35-49). If `yorkieDocKeyPrefix(type)` at line 188 returned the wrong prefix — attaching the copy to a foreign Yorkie key — all sheet tests would still pass.
searchedFor: grep docKeyPrefix across backend spec files

samples.summary: `JSON_ROOT_TYPES` includes 'slides' and 'board' but only 'sheet' is ever exercised
samples.evidence: Every JSON-arm test in document-copy.service.spec.ts uses `SOURCE` with `type: 'sheet'`. No test copies a slides or board document, so a wrong prefix, a root shape those types need (e.g. slides `guides` normalisation, board arrays), or the type ever being dropped from the set is undetected. Nor is there a test for a type that is neither doc/note/JSON/blob (the silent no-op at line 186).

The only comment-stripping test ('does not carry the source’s comment threads into the copy') puts threads at `sheets.t1.comments`. Line 227 (`if (isPlainObject(out.comments)) out.comments = {}`) — the root-level comment map used by non-spreadsheet JSON roots — has no test; deleting that line would leave the suite green. `stripComments` is exported but never imported by the spec.

samples.summary: `reviveLongs` array recursion and the negative out-of-range branch are untested
samples.evidence: The only Long test uses a positive integer nested in an object (`sheets.t1.importedAt`). Nothing covers `Array.isArray(value)` recursion (line 262) with an out-of-range integer inside an array, nor `value < INT32_MIN` (line 258). `reviveLongs` is exported but the spec never imports it directly, so both branches could be removed silently.
searchedFor: big integer literals in the spec

samples.summary: Over-mocking: the JSON-root copy path is never run against a real Yorkie document, so the bigint→Long claim is asserted only against a plain JS object
samples.evidence: The doc/note arms deliberately use real `YorkieDocument` instances (lines 153-190), but the sheet arm writes into `targetRoot: Root = {}` via `update: (fn) => fn(targetRoot)`. `expect(typeof sheets.t1.importedAt).toBe('bigint')` therefore only proves `reviveLongs` returned a BigInt — it cannot show that Yorkie stores it as a Long rather than truncating, which is the stated motivation. The same mock means whole-root assignment of nested objects/arrays onto a real Yorkie root is never exercised.

samples.summary: 'copies sequentially, one request per id, in order' does not detect a parallel implementation
samples.evidence: The mock pushes ids synchronously at call time, so `Promise.all(ids.map(copyDocument))` would produce exactly the same `order` array and the same result order. The only assertion that actually distinguishes sequential from parallel is the *other* test's `expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`. As written, this test's title claims coverage it does not provide (no await ordering/interleaving is observed).

samples.summary: FileService.copy tests restate the implementation expression for `CopySource` instead of the expected literal
samples.evidence: `expect(args.CopySource).toBe(encodeURIComponent('wafflebase-files/wafflebase/aaaaaaaa-1111.png'))` (and line 166) computes the expectation with the exact call the production code makes (file.service.ts:145). If the encoding choice is wrong for the S3 contract (e.g. slashes must not be percent-encoded), both tests still pass. A literal string expectation would make the encoded form visible and falsifiable.

samples.summary: Bare `.toThrow()` / `.rejects.toThrow()` accept any error, including an unintended one
samples.evidence: 'rejects a source whose stored file reference is not a blob id' asserts only `.rejects.toThrow()` — it would pass if the rejection came from an unrelated TypeError rather than the intended `BadRequestException` from the `VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN` guard. Same for `snapshotJsonRoot` line 309 ('rejects a root that is not an object'), which never asserts the 'not an object' message.

samples.summary: The rollback failure paths (deleteDocument rejects, discardBlob rejects) are untested
samples.evidence: 'rolls back the row when the content copy fails' uses a `deleteDocument` mock that resolves, and a source with `fileId: null`, so neither the `.catch(cleanupErr => logger.warn(...))` at lines 111-115 nor `discardBlob`'s swallow-and-log at lines 125-127 is exercised. If either swallow were removed, the cleanup error would escape and mask the original error — no test would catch that.

samples.summary: No test copies a document whose `folderId` is null (workspace root)
samples.evidence: `SOURCE` always has `folderId: 'fld-1'`. The conditional `folder: { connect: ... }` spread (lines 93-95) and the sibling query with `folderId: null` (line 55) — the root-folder case that most workspaces hit — have no test; a copy that mistakenly emits `folder: { connect: { id: null } }` would be caught by neither spec.

samples.summary: No test that a non-member is refused the copy endpoint
samples.evidence: In document.controller.spec.ts the copy suite mocks `assertMember: jest.fn(async () => ({ role }))` — it never rejects, so the only membership coverage is `expect(workspaceService.assertMember).toHaveBeenCalledWith(WS, MEMBER)` (asserting a mock was called). There is no test showing an outsider's `POST /documents/:id/copy` rejects, nor that the copy is not performed when it does.

samples.summary: The new 'Make a copy' UI (menu item, bulk button, partial-failure toast) has no test
samples.evidence: `copyDocumentsMutation`'s success/error toast wording, the `BulkCopyError`-aware 'Copied N, then failed' message, `onSettled` refetch, and the bulk button's visibility (`selectedDocIds.length > 0`, deliberately ungated by `canManage`) are untested. Globbing packages/frontend/src/app/documents/*.test.* returns only miro-import and apply-imported-content tests — document-list.tsx has no spec at all, so this is consistent with the repo, but the gating decision (copy allowed without canManage) is new behavior with no frontend test.

finding.summary: The only test for the `doc` (Tree) copy arm is vacuous — it uses an empty source root and asserts `targetRoot.content` is merely defined
finding.evidence: `it('routes a doc through the Tree serializer rather than a JSON snapshot')` builds the service with `sourceRoot: {}`. In that case `readDocsRoot({})` returns `{ blocks: [] }` (docs-tree.ts:427-431, the `!tree` early return) and `writeDocsRoot` then unconditionally does `root.content = new Tree({type:'doc',children: []})` (docs-tree.ts:524-528). So `targetRoot.content` is defined no matter what was read from the source — the assertion holds even if the read step returned nothing at all, or if the source content were dropped entirely. No test anywhere copies an actual docs document (blocks/inlines/pageSetup/stylesJson) from source to target, so the 'doc' content-transfer behaviour is effectively uncovered while appearing covered.

verdict.reason: The test described by the finding does not exist. Grep across packages/backend/src finds no test named 'routes a doc through the Tree serializer rather than a JSON snapshot' and no `targetRoot.content` / `toBeDefined()` assertion anywhere in document-copy.service.spec.ts (the only `capturedRoot.content).toBeDefined()` hit is in a different file, api/v1/docs-content.controller.spec.ts:220, covering a different behavior). The actual doc-arm test is document-copy.service.spec.ts:131-172, 'carries a doc's blocks through the Tree serializer'. It uses real YorkieDocument instances on both ends (lines 153-155), seeds the source with a genuine DocsDocument containing a block, an inline ('copied text', bold) and a full block style (lines 136-152), and asserts full round-trip equality `expect(readDocsRoot(targetDoc.getRoot())).toEqual(original)` (line 167). Because readDocsRoot returns `{ blocks: [] }` when content is absent/empty (docs-tree.ts:427-431), that assertion fails if the source content is dropped — the opposite of vacuous. It also pins docKeyPrefix 'doc-' on both attaches (lines 169-171), matching document-copy.service.ts:144-162. The finding's secondary claim that no test copies an actual docs document with blocks/inlines is likewise contradicted by the test body; the test's own comment (lines 132-135) explicitly rejects the fake-root/toBeDefined approach the finding attributes to it. The only real residue is that pageSetup/stylesJson (docs-tree.ts:457-466, 540-548) are not exercised in the copy test — coverage breadth on an already-tested arm, minor at most, and not the finding as raised.

finding.summary: New frontend `copyDocument` API function and the whole "Make a copy" UI wiring ship with no test
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` covers `moveDocuments` and `deleteDocuments` (method/URL/body assertions) but has no `copyDocument` case — grep for 'copy' in that file returns nothing. Grep for 'copyDocument'/'Make a copy' across packages/frontend matches only `src/api/documents.ts` and `src/app/documents/document-list.tsx`, i.e. no test file. So the POST verb/URL, the sequential bulk loop, the singular/plural toast, and the deliberate `onSettled` (rather than `onSuccess`) refetch on partial failure — all called out as intentional in the comments — are unverified.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is contradicted by the repository. packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts imports copyDocument/copyDocuments/BulkCopyError (line 10-12) and contains two dedicated describe blocks. describe("copyDocument") at lines 38-62 asserts the POST method (line 47), the /documents/:id/copy URL (line 46), that no body is sent (line 49), and that a server rejection throws the server message (lines 52-61). describe("copyDocuments") at lines 64-89 asserts the sequential loop order (line 75), the returned copies (line 76), and the partial-failure contract that motivates the onSettled refetch: a BulkCopyError carrying already-created copies (lines 84-85) and stopping at the first failure (line 87). The reviewer's grep of that file for 'copy' returning nothing is simply wrong, and their glob 'src/app/documents/*.test.*' missed the __tests__/ subdirectory that holds most tests in that folder. I also verified that comment lines the Grep tool rendered as a single '/' (test line 48, document-list.tsx:558/562) are correct '//' comments when read raw, so the test file parses and the coverage is live. The only untested residual is the toast singular/plural string and onSettled: invalidateLists() inside document-list.tsx:563-585, which is thin declarative react-query wiring whose underlying behavior (BulkCopyError.copied on partial failure) is already tested; that does not meet the rubric bar of a behavior change with no meaningful test.
